160x20.note: fixed-move arm is an exact counterfactual continuation of the baseline

320x40.note: fixed-move arm is an exact counterfactual continuation of the baseline

cross_mesh_ordering_at_production_descen.rationale: 160x20 had 9.0% of its M_nd evolution left, 320x40 had 43.4%. A rule "descend when S < theta" must therefore permit at 160x20 and block at 320x40, which requires S(160x20@78) < S(320x40@129).

normalisation_exponent.derivation: Dividing a count series by the per-mesh constant NE^alpha rescales its admissible-threshold window exactly, so a single threshold works at both meshes iff the count windows overlap after that rescaling, i.e. alpha in [log_R(loB/hiA), log_R(hiB/loA)] with R = NE_320/NE_160 = 4.

predictive_correlation.target: remaining M_nd evolution at move=0.04, rem(k) = Mnd(k) - Mnd(final)
predictive_correlation.method: Spearman rank correlation over the whole fixed-move trajectory
predictive_correlation.note: Positive and large = statistic falls as the topology matures, WITHIN that mesh.

omega1_as_maturity_proxy.question: does omega1 settling imply the topology has finished evolving?

self_normalised_active_set.finding: the peak is reached at iteration 1 where essentially every element moves, so the peak is ~NE and this variant degenerates to the area fraction

markov_cap_tightness.statement: frac(u>=t) <= rmsU^2/t^2 is exact; this is how loose it is in practice
markov_cap_tightness.comparedAgainst: exact frac(|drho|>1e-2) from the move_stop runs

mesh_collapse.method: match the two fixed-move runs at equal M_nd maturity, then find the alpha minimising the RMS log-discrepancy of activeCount/NE^alpha between meshes
mesh_collapse.caveat: ONE exponent fitted to TWO meshes. The band width is fit sensitivity, NOT statistical confidence: two points cannot validate a power law. A third mesh is required and that needs an optimisation run, which this task forbids.

task: offline characterisation of the design-activity signal; NO optimisation run
